questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Forcing myself to get as far away from Denmark as possible. It was quite nice that it was an English speaking country as well, although it was not crucial to me personally.

questions.answer: So many new friends (':

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything was pretty smooth

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any, but if you get in the student accommodation you will be met by a driver at the airport taking you to your place etc. from what I know.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. There are heaps of facebook groups to look for places and the pricing is cheaper than student accom. Would recommend going for the cheaper student accom though, as there are less administrative stuff to take care of and you don't need to find a new tenant when you leave which can be stressful.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you live off campus, you should at least live close to campus. Many events etc. happen there and all your friends will most likely live on campus/right next to. It would have been a pain to live further away than I did as I probably wouldn't have partaken in as many social events etc.

questions.answer: Can barely remember it, which I suggests it was very unproblematic

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A lot of tutors and designated international student help centres

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go with the flow

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level is very different to UCPH. Very oriented towards quizzes and rote learning. I personally found the level much easier than back in Copenhagen, but I assume it is also very dependent on the degree in question.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more like gymnasium than university.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Migration, Culture, Identity - ANTH 317
Te Tiriti o Waitangi - MAOR 216
Sociology of Knowledge - SOSC 307

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sociology of Knowledge and Te Tiriti o Waitangi were very interesting. Particularly MAOR 216 which gives you some very nice insight to the relationship between Pakeha and Maori. It can be difficult to follow in the beginning as there is a certain implicit native knowledge to New Zealanders but the teachers are very good at explaining and taking questions regarding it.

questions.answer: Food is expensive in Wellington!

questions.answer: Avocados are dirt cheap. Tomatoes are quite expensive. Also cigarettes are unimaginably expensive

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Football, volleyball, badminton, yoga, tramping, kayaking, chess you name it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hang out with the other exchange students as much as possible.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Nature road trips! It's amazing

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: 10/10 easy. Basically Europe/UK

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The local students are usually very much in their own groups. Would direct my time towards other exchange students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They vape A LOT

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Attempts at returning to Maori indigeneity.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Spend as much time as you possibly can with the other exchange students - you don't know when you'll see them again.
Don't take the academic stuff too seriously, it's much more doable than back home - prioritise social and nature experiences!
Be prepared to walk uphill!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's pretty chill

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and making friends for life

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning to find a way in the social network of so many new people. But after that: saying goodbye to the wonderful people I met.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Going on exchange is AMAZING - go for it!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
